li.a: SBS News: Former WA bikie fined $15,000 for lying
The Nightly: Danny Makin, Coffin Cheaters bikie dies in car crash near Bindoon
The West Australian: Violent times in reign of bikie gangs
1News: Mongrel Mob gangsters deported back to NZ from Western Australia
Bayside News: Police raid bikies' bases
Dandenong Star Journal: Police raid alleged OMCG clubhouse

content.p: The Coffin Cheaters are an outlaw motorcycle club based in Western Australia, with members in Victoria. For decades they were one of the four big clubs in the state, and newspaper reports link their name to brawls, drug raids and prosecutions, and to a violent 1989 dispute in Perth. The reporting here comes from police statements, court reports and local newspapers. None of it is a trial of the club as a whole, and some of the detail below is given by one outlet and not repeated by another.

The West Australian's 2010 retrospective on the state's bikie gangs describes a 1970s and 1980s in which four clubs expanded with little interference: the God's Garbage, based in Albany; the Gypsy Jokers, based in Maddington; Club Deroes, whose headquarters were in Cloverdale; and the Coffin Cheaters, whose home was Bayswater. The Cheaters also set up chapters in Bunbury and Fremantle. Smaller clubs were folded into the bigger ones after a run through the south-west that the newspaper called messy.

The club's most visible public event was the Bindoon Rock Festival, a rollicking weekend of music and camping that ran from 1986 to 1995 and drew tens of thousands of people over two days. The West Australian reports that the festival involved some co-operation with WA Police to keep it running. A police sergeant, Frank Scott, later wrote a report saying drugs were supplied and sold at the concerts, and asking how the department could allow it. The newspaper reports that Scott was discharged from the force after a 22-year career and became a whistleblower in media reports. The club rejects his claims. Edward Horace Withnell, who the newspaper describes as the biggest name in WA motorcycle gang history, later wrote to the Liquor Licensing Commission of WA that Scott had "thrown a tissy fit" at the concert.

Police, according to the same article, believed the big four were moving into organised crime, including substantial drug deals. They were especially worried about the Coffin Cheaters, and about the money and connections the club had made at Bindoon.
content.h2: The 1989 clash with the Mongrel Mob
content.p: The four Western Australian clubs were unhappy when the Mongrel Mob opened a chapter in Perth. The New Zealand gang had a reputation for violence at home, and the Western Australian clubs objected to its move into minor organised crime, which the newspaper says included fencing stolen electrical items and selling drugs. According to The West Australian, the four clubs had Withnell as their spokesman.

The newspaper describes a week of violence in late 1989. Its account says the Perth chapter's vice-president, Selwyn Wharepapa, who ran a motorcycle repair shop in Midvale, was the main target. It reports that the shop was firebombed by a Gypsy Joker, and that Wharepapa was later shot outside his home in Swan View by a Gypsy Joker riding in a car driven by a God's Garbage member. These are the newspaper's accounts; it does not say that any of these men was convicted of those acts, so they are given here as reported. Several Western Australian gang members were arrested that week, according to the same article.

Asked whether he condoned the shooting, Withnell told the paper: "We live in very real times, and some people are thrust to the front line of a very real situation." The Mongrel Mob left Perth after a Kiwi member, Michael "Pixie" Moke, negotiated the terms of the surrender with Withnell, the newspaper reports. Its comment on the backdown was blunt: one New Zealand police officer said gang members going to Australia were "like babes coming into an adult world".

According to 1News, the Mongrel Mob was still reportedly trying to establish a foothold in the state years later. In March 2018, it reported on a Weekend West report that at least five members had been deported from the state over the previous year. Among them was senior member Joe Edmonds, whose visa was cancelled on character grounds after he was caught trying to bring gang regalia into the country in his luggage. The Weekend West said several Mongrel Mob members remained in Perth and were being watched by police. A "Mongrel Mob Australia" page had been set up, but it had not been updated since November 2015, according to the NZ Herald as cited by 1News.
content.h2: The 2010 brawl and the corruption hearings
content.p: The best-documented episode in the club's recent history is a brawl at a motorplex in October 2010. SBS News reports that it took place at the Kwinana Motorplex and involved members of the Finks and the Coffin Cheaters. The Nightly places it at the Perth Motorplex and says the melee, which drew in about 20 people, began with a spitting incident during a drag race meeting between a Finks man and a Coffin Cheater. Several Coffin Cheaters, according to The Nightly, ran from different parts of the venue to join the fight. The Nightly reports that Finks member Stephen Wallace had three fingers severed, which were reattached in surgery, and that David Marrapodi suffered a gunshot wound to the leg.

The Corruption and Crime Commission held a private hearing to help a police investigation into the fight. SBS reports that Aaron Dinesh John, 30, told the hearing he did not see an altercation even though he had been photographed at the incident. John admitted lying to the commission. In the Perth Magistrates Court he was fined $15,000, the second person in a week to be fined for the same offence. SBS reports that the court was told John was no longer associated with the Coffin Cheaters.

Danny Sydney Makin was the first of the two. The Nightly reports that he also told the hearing he had not seen a fight, that he admitted in 2013 that he had lied, and that he was fined $15,000. SBS reports that Makin was fined the week before John.

The two outlets give different dates for the hearing. SBS says the private hearing was in 2010, while The Nightly says Makin was grilled by the commission in 2011. The reports do not settle which is right.

The Nightly reports that Makin, then 49, died on 13 April after the car he was driving hit a tree north of Perth. No one else was in the car, and he died at the scene. The paper quotes an obituary in The West Australian in which his family described him as "forever in our hearts". An online comment on the obituary, believed to come from the Gypsy Jokers, called him a "well respected and outstanding contributor" to the outlaw scene. Police said they were continuing to investigate the crash and asked anyone with dash-cam or phone footage to come forward. The Nightly's report was published in May 2024, and it gives no more detail on the cause of the crash.

Members of the club in Victoria have also drawn police attention. In August 2015, police served search warrants on several properties linked to the Coffin Cheaters, including addresses in Parkdale and Aspendale and a factory in Braeside, Bayside News reports. A Caulfield Divisional Response Unit carried out the searches as part of an inquiry into alleged drug dealing and liquor offences. The paper said the raids allegedly uncovered drugs, weapons, cash and a large amount of liquor. A 58-year-old Windsor man was arrested and was assisting police with inquiries.

Inspector John Cormack, of Southern Division Investigations, told the paper that police believed the club had been running a premises without a liquor licence. "Our investigation has identified a factory in Braeside which includes a purpose-built bar," he said. "We believe the bar is a place of assembly for the Coffin Cheaters and their associates."

In the early morning of 3 November 2023, detectives from Echo Taskforce, working with the Special Operations Group, VIPER and the Dog Squad, raided clubhouses in four towns: Dandenong, Braeside, Morwell and Warragul, the Dandenong Star Journal reports. A 68-year-old man from Dandenong was cautioned for drug possession, and police said he is alleged to be a patched Coffin Cheaters member. Searches also turned up suspected cannabis and knuckle dusters. Earlier, police had charged three men living in Truganina, Armstrong Creek and Cairnlea over alleged threats, assaults and an affray in Melbourne's west.

Detective Inspector Mick Daly of Echo Taskforce said: "This kind of unacceptable violent behaviour from OMCGs is cowardly and it will not be tolerated." He added: "If you are involved in organised criminal activity of any nature, rest assured, you will be held to account no matter where you are." The investigation was still ongoing when the report was published.

The reporting used here does not give the club's founding year, or say how far it spread beyond Western Australia and Victoria. Accounts of the 1989 violence come mainly from one newspaper retrospective, and the arrests it describes are not tied to convictions. The dates of the 2010 hearings differ between SBS and The Nightly, and the two reports name the venue differently. Anyone reading about the club should keep these gaps in mind, and treat the police and court statements as the firmest ground.
